assumptions_named: One assumption was load-bearing and is now named: THAT THE AUTHORITY REFUSAL WAS DOING WORK. It is not. cairn/harbor_master/clearance.py:1 compares `actor != boat_owner` and both values arrive from the SAME caller in the SAME call, so any caller can make them equal — including a caller with no standing at all. Measured 2026-08-10 during the first live fire of clear(): the very first production call refused as Unauthorized because the settlement had put boat_owner in the component namespace ('base'), and the fix that made it pass was to type a different string. A check a caller can satisfy by choosing its arguments is a declaration, not a refusal. Second assumption, examined and DISCHARGED: that the grant path rescues it — it does not, because Grant.authorizes() checks `by_owner == owner` where `owner` is again the caller-supplied boat_owner, so a caller who can state boat_owner can mint itself a grant from that same fictional owner.
still_open_at_cast: One point I would have asserted wrapped and is not: WHERE the boat's owner is read FROM. The boat is the ticket (boat_id is the ticket id on every gated crossing), so the ticket file is the obvious address — but the ticket's existing `owner` field is PROSE about which COMPONENT owns which rung ('harbor_master owns the AUTHORITY rung; base owns THE DOOR'), which is exactly the namespace confusion this ticket exists to fix, one layer up. So the field cannot simply be read; either it gains a machine-readable sibling naming a MOVER, or the boat's owner lives somewhere else. That is a real open question and it is child (a) rather than smuggled past. Everything else is wrapped: the defect is measured, the mechanism is one comparison at one address, and the corrected settlement is already written beside it.
